## GamblerNet
Larger reward encourages predictions, while lower reward intends to abstain.

Exps:


```{python}
from great_tables import GT,html
import pandas as pd

Exps = pd.DataFrame({
    'Reward': [1.2, 1.4, 1.8, 2.0],
    'Pretrained': ['No', 'No', '40', '40']
})

GT(Exps)

# 打印表格
```

## SelectiveNet

::: {layout="[80,-2,40]" layout-valign="center"}
![Structure of SelectiveNet ](./SENet.png){#fig-SelectiveNet}

Target: Given a target coverage, minimize the loss


:::

Selective loss function:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{(f,g)} \triangleq \hat{r}_e(f, g|\mathcal{S}_m) + \lambda \Psi(c - \phi(g|\mathcal{S}_m))
$$
Emprical loss function:
$$
\hat{r}(f, g|\mathcal{S}_m) \triangleq \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} \frac{\ell(f(x_i), y_i)g(x_i)}{\phi(g|\mathcal{S}_m)} 
$$
Emprical coverage:
$$
\hat{\phi}(g|\mathcal{S}_m) \triangleq \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} g(x_i).
$$


##
::: {style="font-size: 200%"}
How to choose the threshold?
:::
Assumption: 
- Larger selection head output means more confident to predict
- Coverage around target coverage can represent performance of optimization

## Results--SelectiveNet
Can we find an appropriate threshold?

::: {layout=[40,-2,40] layout-valign="center"  #fig-performance}
![Train-coverage:0.7](./C_7.png){#fig-Performanceunderdifferentthreshold}

![Train-coverage:0.5](./C_8.png){#fig-Performanceunderdifferentthreshold}

Performance under different thresholds
:::

Show potential that larger selection value means better predictions

Coverage rates vary in different fold

But why? Emprical coverage is represented by average of g(x), then larger g(x) is more likely to be predicted?

$$
\hat{\phi}(g|\mathcal{S}_m) \triangleq \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} g(x_i).
$$

When batch size = 1, emprical risk equals to normal CELoss?
